name: Wearable Mechanisms & Exoskeletons
summary: Designing machines worn on the body, from passive supports to powered exoskeletons and suits, with emphasis on human-machine joints and interfaces.

topics.name: Exoskeleton and exosuit classes: passive/active, upper/lower body, industrial, medical, military
Deriving requirements from human biomechanics: joint torques, powers and ranges of motion
Human-machine joint alignment: misalignment, self-aligning and remote-centre-of-motion mechanisms
Physical human-robot interface: cuffs, straps, pressure distribution and skin comfort
Load paths, load transfer to the ground and body-weight support
Actuation and transmission choices for wearables (cable-driven, series elastic, hydraulic)
Control: transparency, assist-as-needed, impedance and admittance control
Intent detection: EMG, IMUs, force sensing and gait-phase estimation
Evaluation: metabolic cost, kinematics and user acceptance
Power, thermal and mass budgets for full-body powered suits
